mechanism_narrative: The ongoing decline in WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL rise implies weaker weekday commuting and more at-home substitution, which depresses discretionary retail visits. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above the previous 28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below their current 4-week averages and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each fall further for one week, the resulting loss of out-of-home routines reduces incidental shopping and restaurant trips within 1 to 2 weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC lower than the last month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 while WORKPLACES stays below -14 on a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses below -20 and WORKPLACES remains below -14 on weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES while RESIDENTIAL rises creates a stronger stay-at-home substitution effect than either series alone, which should produce a four-week decline in RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying weak and RESIDENTIAL remaining above baseline.
